concerns.text: FR-010 mandates capping the dataset to '[deferred] of the original size'. The placeholder '[deferred]' is not a measurable value. A requirement cannot be verified if the threshold is undefined. The spec must resolve this to a concrete percentage (e.g., '10%') or explicitly reference the plan's resolved value to be testable.

The Edge Cases section repeats the '[deferred]' placeholder for the sample cap ('capped at [deferred] of the original'). This makes the edge-case handling untestable. The specific cap value must be defined here to verify the system's behavior under memory constraints.

FR-011 requires computing 'interference distance' by measuring recall drop when 'semantically unrelated items' are assigned to 'adjacent grid coordinates'. The spec does not define the algorithm for identifying 'semantically unrelated items' or the mechanism for 'adjacent' assignment. Without a defined injection protocol, this metric cannot be computed or verified.

US-3 Acceptance Scenario 1 requires 'injecting semantically unrelated items' but fails to specify the mechanism for determining 'unrelatedness' or the 'adjacent' condition. This leaves the test procedure ambiguous and unverifiable.

FR-003 states the system MUST reduce batch size if 'peak memory usage exceeds 6 GB RAM'. It does not define the measurement point (e.g., per-batch RSS, epoch peak) or the exact threshold logic (>6.0 vs >=6.0). This ambiguity prevents deterministic verification of the trigger condition.

FR-005 requires 'paired two-tailed t-tests' but does not explicitly state the null hypothesis (e.g., 'mean difference = 0'). While 'two-tailed' implies a direction, the explicit hypothesis statement is required for statistical verifiability.

FR-006 requires family-wise error correction 'when >1 hypothesis test is run'. It does not define the scope of 'tests' (e.g., across 3 datasets, across seeds, or both). This ambiguity makes the correction logic untestable.

FR-007 requires 'Cohen's d effect size with 95% confidence intervals' but does not specify the formula (e.g., pooled SD vs. SD of difference) or the CI calculation method (e.g., non-central t-distribution). Different valid methods yield different results, making the requirement untestable without a specific definition.

FR-008 requires logging 'slot occupancy distribution' but does not define the output format (e.g., histogram bins, list of counts, mean/std). Without a defined format, the log data cannot be consistently verified or compared.
FR-009 requires logging 'coordinate variance' but does not specify if this is x-variance, y-variance, or 2D covariance trace. This ambiguity makes the requirement untestable.

SC-006 states success requires a 'statistically significant reduction in interference' but does not explicitly reference the alpha threshold (e.g., p < 0.05). While SC-004 defines alpha, SC-006 must explicitly link to it to be a self-contained, measurable success criterion.

The Assumptions section contains a fragmented sentence with unresolved placeholders: '[Citation]', '[Research Question]', and '[Method]'. This text is grammatically broken and leaves the basis for interference thresholds and batch size logic undefined, rendering the spec untestable in this section.

FR-001 requires a '2-D grid of memory slots' but does not specify the grid dimensions (e.g., 8x8). While an assumption mentions 8x8, the functional requirement itself is incomplete without the dimension constraint, making the implementation scope ambiguous.
